approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (The Survivors Law) Bill 2026

Argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (The Survivors Law) Bill 2026 should pass swiftly, supporting survivors of child sexual abuse by enabling access to certain perpetrator superannuation, preserving compensation debts through bankruptcy and addressing a loophole that has allowed assets to be shielded from court orders.

Supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (The Survivors Law) Bill 2026, arguing it would prevent perpetrators of child sexual abuse from shielding assets in superannuation or using bankruptcy to avoid court-ordered compensation; the bill permits access to certain contributions after 12 months and establishes enforcement safeguards.

Moved that government business, including five specified bills and a related bill subject to introduction, be considered from 12.15 pm until no later than 1.30 pm, followed by general business notice of motion no. 510 concerning the 2026-27 Budget. The question was agreed to.
Treasury Laws Amendment (The Survivors Law) Act 2026
